newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on speculative buying.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Friday on speculative buying from retail investors, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 21,880 yuan ($2637.89) per tonne, rising 80 yuan. It opened at 21,820 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 21,790 and a high of 21,900.
February rose 160 to 21,590, March 170 to 21,650, April 140 to 21,760, and June 130 to 21,880. The July and August contracts did not trade.
Combined volume rose to 28,380 tonnes from 21,390.
Copper opened high and stayed high for most of the session.
Traders said retail investors dominated today's trading but the market trend was still unclear.
"Many investors were taking a wait-and-see attitude and did not want to build fresh positions with the long Chinese lunar new year holiday approaching," one trader said.
"This speculative buying does not represent a mid- or long-term trend," he added.
Analysts said copper futures would be supported by spot prices hovering around 21,300 per tonne, but sharp rises were unlikely.
"Too many investors want to reduce risk by liquidating long positions at high levels," one analyst said.
Aluminium ended up. February rose 20 to 15,400, March 130 to 15,730, April 110 to 15,910 and May 100 to 16,100.
Combined volume rose to 2,410 tonnes from 690.
